review.scope: Public class over Resolver's InetNameResolver. Resolver API policy (docs/resolver-porting-manifest.json contractPolicy): resolve/resolveAll/query are Task-returning ResolveAsync/ResolveAllAsync/QueryAsync with a CancellationToken (Future<InetAddress> Task<IPAddress>, Future<List<InetAddress>> Task<IReadOnlyList<IPAddress>>, Future<List<DnsRecord>> Task<IReadOnlyList<IDnsRecord>>, Future<AddressedEnvelope<DnsResponse, InetSocketAddress>> Task<IAddressedEnvelope<IDnsResponse, IPEndPoint>>, the covariant codec-dns envelope); every overload that takes a Promise folds into the Task-returning overload with its original comments beside it, the protected doResolve/doResolveAll hooks that complete a caller's Promise are the Task-returning DoResolveAsync/DoResolveAllAsync(inetHost, additionals, cache, token), and close() is Dispose(). The caller's CancellationToken stands for Future.cancel(...): CancellationToken.Register ("run immediately and synchronously" when already canceled, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.cancellationtoken.register?view=net-10.0) calls TrySetCanceled (false once "already in one of the three final states", https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.taskcompletionsource-1.trysetcanceled?view=net-10.0) on the caller's promise, which the resolve contexts read as isCancelled(). Promise is a TaskCompletionSource with RunContinuationsAsynchronously and Future its Task (docs/handler-porting.md, "Promise, ChannelPromise, Future"); isDone()/isCancelled()/isSuccess() are Task.IsCompleted/IsCanceled/IsCompletedSuccessfully, trySuccess/tryFailure TrySetResult/TrySetException, setSuccess/setFailure SetResult/SetException (InvalidOperationException for a completed promise, IllegalStateException in Java), cancel(false) TrySetCanceled() and cause() DnsNameResolver.Cause (the inner exception of a faulted Task, a TaskCanceledException for a canceled one). Listeners are continuations on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over the event loop, which runs them at once on the loop and otherwise through the executor, the DefaultPromise.notifyListeners() timing (src/Netty.NET.Common/Concurrent/EventExecutorTaskScheduler.cs); an exception thrown by a listener faults its continuation Task where DefaultPromise logs it (https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/64cc10f38ea5f5bd7eae48507817c66680d0afdc/common/src/main/java/io/netty/util/concurrent/DefaultPromise.java). In doQuery's consolidation the release listener is executed through the executor because a continuation added to a completed Task runs at once (inline on the event loop), where DefaultPromise appends a listener added during notification after the listeners being notified; the release therefore still follows the other waiters' retains. When the channel is not ready, query(...) returns the caller's promise Task in place of the second promise that PromiseNotifier.cascade fills from it (https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/64cc10f38ea5f5bd7eae48507817c66680d0afdc/common/src/main/java/io/netty/util/concurrent/PromiseNotifier.java; "Share the same read-only Task when appropriate", docs/common-task-composition.md). ChannelFactory<? extends DatagramChannel/SocketChannel> is Func<IDatagramChannel>/Func<ISocketChannel>, ChannelFuture the Task<IChannel> of Bootstrap.RegisterAsync/BindAsync/ConnectAsync and ChannelPromise the Task that a channel write returns (docs/transport-porting.md). A faulted Task<IChannel> has no channel (docs/transport-porting.md), so the transport setup failure message ends after "couldn't setup transport" and DnsResolveChannelPerResolverProvider.close() closes the channel when the registration completes. executor() with the covariant EventLoop return is a protected internal Executor property hiding SimpleNameResolver.Executor; package-private members are internal (newRedirectServerAddress internal virtual, overridden by the tests of the package), the protected newRedirectDnsServerStream is protected internal virtual (DnsResolveContext calls it; a friend test assembly overrides it with protected internal override, measured: CS0507 otherwise) and the two public constructors, @deprecated "Use {@link DnsNameResolverBuilder}", are not ported (comment recorded). AttributeKey<Boolean> is AttributeKey<object> with a boxed bool (as src/Netty.NET.Handler/Traffic/AbstractTrafficShapingHandler.cs); the deprecated DATAGRAM_CHANNEL_ACTIVE_ON_REGISTRATION ([Obsolete] in Transport) is used under the constructor's @SuppressWarnings("deprecation") as #pragma warning disable CS0612. The anonymous ChannelHandlerAdapter, DatagramDnsResponseDecoder ([Sharable] inherited, src/Netty.NET.Transport/Channels/IChannelHandler.cs) and ChannelInitializer are nested classes; anonymous Runnables/listeners are lambdas. Static initializer: InetAddress.getLocalHost().getHostName() (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/net/InetAddress.html) is Dns.GetHostName(), "Gets the host name of the local computer" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.dns.gethostname?view=net-10.0); getSearchDomainsHack() keeps only its Java 9+ result (an empty list), its PlatformDependent.javaVersion() < 9 branch reading sun.net.dns.ResolverConfiguration by reflection is not ported (comments recorded, jvm-only-replaced); anyInterfaceSupportsIpV6() reads GetIPProperties().UnicastAddresses (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.networkinformation.ipinterfaceproperties.unicastaddresses?view=net-10.0) with IPv6Any (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.ipaddress.ipv6any?view=net-10.0), IPAddress.IsLoopback (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.ipaddress.isloopback?view=net-10.0) and IsIPv6LinkLocal (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.ipaddress.isipv6linklocal?view=net-10.0); Arrays.toString is ArraysToString, "[a, b]" (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Arrays.html). Class<? extends InetAddress> is the AddressFamily? of the address (Inet4Address.class InterNetwork, null for UNIX), as infra's NameServerComparator takes it. Collections.sort of the redirect name servers is stable (https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Collections.html) and is Enumerable.OrderBy, which "performs a stable sort" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.linq.enumerable.orderby?view=net-10.0), written back (SortStable). caseMappings.adaptation: The FutureListener is a continuation on Common's EventExecutorTaskScheduler over the configured loop: a Task has no executor (SimpleNameResolver: Tasks do not impose executor affinity), so the continuation is put on the loop that notifies the resolver future's listeners in Java (DefaultPromise on the resolver's executor, which DnsAddressResolverGroup.newResolver picks as the configured loop); loop.inEventLoop() then holds by that construction, and UnsupportedAddressTypeException is Resolver's counterpart (an ArgumentException).

TestDnsServer (the apacheds DnsServer subclass with the AAAA hack, the dropped record type, filterMessage and the MapRecordStoreA/TestRecordStore/TestResourceRecord helpers) and the ApacheDs/ stand-in of apacheds-protocol-dns 2.0.0.AM27 and Apache MINA 2.2.3 it runs on. Owner decision 2026-11-25 (user: "C# 대체 서버 구현"): TestDnsServer extends the apacheds-protocol-dns 2.0.0.AM27 DnsServer on Apache MINA 2.2.3 (the MINA version apacheds pins, https://github.com/apache/directory-server/blob/2.0.0.AM27/pom.xml), so it is ported on a test-only C# stand-in of exactly the apacheds/MINA API that TestDnsServer, DnsNameResolverTest, SearchDomainTest, DnsAddressResolverGroupTest and IsolatedDnsNameResolverTest use, in ApacheDs/ (namespace Netty.NET.Resolver.Dns.Tests.ApacheDs, the counterpart of the org.apache.directory.server.* and org.apache.mina.* imports): the same type names (interfaces with the I prefix), Java member names, one file per type, each with a // CLR: header naming the apacheds/MINA source it reproduces and its GitHub URL at the pinned tag. No jar or package is added. The stand-in reproduces the apacheds wire behaviour the tests depend on, read from the sources: DnsMessageDecoder decodes names without the trailing root dot, only A/NS/MX/AAAA records and throws for an EDNS OPT record (so a query with OPT gets no response, which is why the tests disable optResourceEnabled); DomainNameService answers NAME_ERROR for a null or empty RecordStore result and copies the id, RD flag and questions; DnsProtocolHandler answers a DnsException with its response code and closes the session without a response for any other exception; DnsMessageEncoder counts every record but writes only SOA/A/NS/CNAME/PTR/MX/SRV/TXT (an AAAA record is skipped with a logged IOException), which is what TestDnsServer's AAAA hack appends after the last section. MINA is reproduced as far as the server needs it: NioDatagramAcceptor binds a BCL UDP socket (SO_REUSEADDR from the session config, IOException on bind failure), runs one receive thread, keeps one session per remote address whose filter chain carries the codec that sessionCreated adds, copies each datagram into a 2048-byte IoBuffer (DatagramChannel.receive discards the rest), and sends the encoded IoBuffer back; ProtocolCodecFilter asks the factory for a codec per message and sends nothing when the encoder writes nothing; IoBuffer has the java.nio.Buffer position/limit rules over a byte[]. The server is built on BCL sockets rather than codec-dns because the tests depend on the apacheds encoder/decoder quirks above, which codec-dns does not have (its DefaultDnsRecordEncoder writes AAAA records in place, which would break the AAAA hack); codec-dns is the client side, as in the resolver. Not reproduced (no caller): the LDAP-backed DnsServer.start() (Start() throws NotSupportedException; TestDnsServer overrides it), the TCP transport and codec, ExpiringSessionRecycler expiry, idle events, write futures and queues, and DnsMessage.equals/hashCode. Selfcheck (19 xUnit tests outside the project, scratch build) queried the server with codec-dns over UDP and the TCP replay path: A, AAAA through the hack (and its append-after-all-sections order), MX, CNAME+A order, TXT, SRV, NS/A authority/additional added by filterMessage, NXDOMAIN, REFUSED from DnsException, no response for a dropped record type, a null filterMessage result, a non-DnsException store failure and an OPT record, the truncated flag, two servers side by side, stop(), and the DnsMessageEncoder/IoBuffer TCP replay of DnsNameResolverTest.responseViaSocket.
